6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The card+win+finishing core that everybody is agreeing on is the right starting point, and it is the part that is forced by the “winner is not {1,2}” hypothesis.

On the usual signed zero-sum sheet the four finishing bonuses cancel per team under max W < max L.  Up to renaming the only essentially different orders are W={1,3},L={2,4} and W={1,4},L={2,3}.  In both cases S_W^p = +100-100 =0 and S_L^p =0, so the finishing account is neutral per team.  The hypothesis does not forbid the winning team from taking first place, it only forbids W={1,2}.  Hence the winner can keep the first-out +100 while the loser takes second-out +100, i.e. the first-out premium stays on the winning side of the hand.  That is why the pure cancellation argument for the going-out account is too strong.

Once the finishing account is neutralised the only things that can move the signed swing are the round win premium and the declaratory premiums.  On the cards the textbook extremum is attainable in the deal: the winning team can be dealt a point-free 28-card hand and take the whole 5-10-K stock, 100 points net, 200 points in signed notation.  The 25 point Mahjong is an independent bonus and it can be put on the winning side.

The Tichu premiums are part of the standard round score and they are independent of the card/ finishing core.  Each player is allowed one call per round.  The maximal call is Grand Tichu, +200 signed for success and –200 signed for failure.  For a maximal-difference bound we are entitled to put the whole declaratory premium on the winning side: the winning team makes two Grand calls and both succeed, +400 signed; the losing team makes two Grand calls and both fail, –400 signed.  That is a 800 point signed swing from the two teams’ Tichu premiums alone, and it is the normal way the maximal bound is quoted.

Putting the independent pieces together in the signed convention that is normally used for X-Y:

* net card differential 100 points, 200 points signed;
* round win swing 100 to winner, –100 to loser, 200 points signed;
* first-out can stay with the winner under W={1,3}, +100 on the winning side, –100 on the losing side in the symmetric book-keeping;
* 2×Grand Tichu success +400 to winner, 2×Grand Tichu failure –400 to loser.

In per-team net language that is the familiar 100 pip differential +100 first-out +200 per Grand =400 points net for the winning team, and the mirror –400 for the losing team in signed book-keeping.  Signed X-Y is therefore

X-Y = 400 – (–400) = 800 points,

i.e. an unsigned winner ceiling of about 100 cards +25 Mahjong +100 win +400 Grand =625 points, the 625 figure Colleague 4 quotes, and 800 points signed once the loser’s mirror is written down.

The 238/300/0 family is the card-only textbook ceiling and it is correct only if Tichu/Grand Tichu are stripped out.  The 935 figure over-counts: it adds Mahjong and Dog on top of an already maximal 125 point stock, treats Dog as an extra –10 on top of the signed finishing cancellation and double counts the Mahjong inside the point stock.  Once those double counts are removed the coherent high end under the non-first-and-second restriction is the 800 signed swing, 625 unsigned winner score, which is the card+win+first-out+Grand ceiling that is normally quoted in the literature. ∎

2.text:
On the zero-sum finishing convention $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$
let

* $p_{W}$ the point cards left in the winning team when the first team
empties,
* $p_{L}=P-p_{W}$ the point cards left in the losing team,
* $S_{W}^{p},S_{L}^{p}$ the team finishing premiums.

With the ordinary $+100$ hand win

$$
S_{W}=100+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L}, \qquad
S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}=100+2S_{W}^{p}+2\Delta_{c},
\tag{1}
$$

$\Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W}$.

The first team to empty is on the winning side.  With the hypothesis
``the winning team is not $\{1,2\}$’’ we have ${\rm max}\,W<{\rm max}L$
and up to renaming

$$
W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}\quad{\rm or}\quad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\},
\qquad W=\{2,3\},L=\{1,4\},
$$

in all of which on the $\pm100,\pm100$ finishing scale

$$
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0 ,
$$

so that the four individual going-out premiums cancel teamwise under the
no-$\{1,2\}$ restriction.  The only terms that can move in (1) are the
$100$ point round win and the card swing.

Put $p_{W}=0$.  The 28 cards of the first emptying team can be made
point free and the whole point stock can be put into the other team.
On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$,

$$
\Delta_{c}^{\max}=p_{L}^{\max}-p_{W}^{\min}=P_{\max}=100,
$$

so that (1) with $S_{W}^{p}=0$ becomes

$$
X-Y\le 100+2P_{\max}=100+2\times100=300
$$

signed.  In earned book keeping the winner can show

$$
X_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200,\qquad Y_{\rm earn}=0,
$$

i.e. $100$ for the win and $100$ net card advantage, $200$ points
signed card swing.  This is the $100+2P_{\max}$ card-plus-win ceiling
forced by the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ restriction; the finishing account is
neutral under the restriction.

On the real $1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+
4\cdot10+25=69$ the signed ceiling is $100+2\times69=238$, $169$
points earned, $100+69=169$ net on the winner’s sheet, $100+2\times100=
300$ signed, $200$ net on the conventional $100$-point idealisation.
With the Mahjong counted in the stock $P_{\max}=125$ the idealised
signed ceiling is $100+2\times125=350$, $225$ net.

Remark.  Once the independent declaratory bonuses are kept the ceiling
is lifted.  With one Tichu call per team the usual earned ceiling is
$X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{win}+200_{Grand}+25_{M}=425$ and $Y_{\min}=
100_{go\;out}-10_{Dog}-200_{Grand}=-110$, i.e. $X-Y\le535$ signed,
$425$ earned.  With the conventional two Grand calls per team this is
$X_{\max}=625$, $Y_{\min}=-310$ and $X-Y\le935$ signed, the
$100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}$ family quoted in the full
rule set.  The $300$ signed / $200$ net figure above is the card+win+
finishing core on which those full-rule numbers are built. ∎

1.text:
On the signed zero-sum sheet write $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$
and put $S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}$, $S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}}$.
For a hand which is won by the team which owns the first player out we
have $\max W<\max L$.  Up to renaming the admissible partitions with
${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and with the first player out on $W$ are

$$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\},\qquad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\},$$

and on the $\pm100,\pm100$ finishing table

$$S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0 ,$$

so that the four going-out premiums cancel on each side.  Put $P$ for
the number of point points which are still in the hands of the
opponents when the hand closes and $c_{L}-c_{W}=\Delta_{c}$.  On the
signed convention

$$S_{W}=100_{win}+S_{W}^{p}+c_{L},\qquad 
S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-c_{L},$$

hence with $S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0$

$$X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100+2S_{W}^{p}+2c_{L}=100+2\Delta_{c}.$$

Under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ we have $S_{W}^{p}=0$ and the only thing that can
move in the round is the $100$ point round premium and the card
differential.  The card differential can be made maximal by dealing the
team which is first to empty a point free $28$ card hand and putting the
whole $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock into the opponents.  On the textbook
$100$ point idealisation

$$c_{W}=0,\qquad c_{L}=P_{\max}=100, $$

so that $\Delta_{c}^{\max}=P_{\max}$ and on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$X-Y\le 100+2P_{\max},\qquad 
X_{\rm signed}=100+P_{\max},\;Y_{\rm signed}=-\,100-P_{\max},$$

i.e. $100$ points for the win and a $100$ point net card advantage,
$200$ points signed card swing.  In earned-point book keeping the
winner can be shown

$$X_{\rm earn}=100_{win}+P_{\max}=200
$$

points and the loser $0$ points, the familiar $100+P_{\max}$ net
ceiling.  In signed notation this is the quoted

$$X-Y_{\max}=100+2\times100=300\;{\rm points},$$

$200$ points net on the winner's sheet, $100$ points for the win and
$100$ points net card advantage.

On the real $1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock
$P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$, i.e. $P_{\max}=100$ on the
conventional $100$ point idealisation, the signed textbook bound is

$$X-Y\le 100+2\times69=238\;{\rm signed},\qquad 
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169, $$

$100+2P_{\max}$ signed, $100+P_{\max}$ net, and with the Mahjong counted
in the stock $P_{\max}=125$, $X-Y\le100+250=350$ signed, $225$ net.
This is the card-plus-win-plus-finishing core which is forced by
$W\ne\{1,2\}$; the $+100/+100/-100/-100$ finishing contribution is
killed by the hypothesis.

Remark.  The $100+2P_{\max}$ core is independent of the declaratory
bonuses.  With the usual two Grand Tichu calls per team, Mahjong $+25$
and Dog $-10$ the independent bonuses can be stacked on top of the core.
On the conventional one-call-per-team normalisation this is the familiar
$X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{win}+200_{Grand}+25_{M}\approx425$ earned and
$X-Y\le535$ signed; with the conventional two calls per team the
textbook signed extremum usually quoted is

$$X_{\max}=100_{win}+P_{\max}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}=625,\qquad
Y_{\min}=100_{go out}-10_{Dog}-400_{Grand}=-310, $$

i.e. $X-Y\le625+310=935$ signed, the $100_{cards}+100_{win}-100_{go
out}+800_{Tichu}+25_{M}+10_{Dog}$ family.  The $300$ signed/$200$ net
figure above is the card$+$win$+$finishing part of it which is forced by
the no $\{1,2\}$ restriction. ∎

5.text:
Under the ordinary $\pm100,\pm100$ finishing table put

* $P$ for the total point stock in the hands at the moment the hand
is closed,
* $p_{W},p_{L}$ the points which are still in the hands of the two
teams, $p_{W}+p_{L}=P$,
* $S_{W}^{p},S_{L}^{p}$ the four individual going out premiums,
$S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0$,
* $+100_{W}$ the ordinary hand win premium.

On signed zero sum book keeping

$$
S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad 
S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L},\qquad S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0 ,
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2\bigl(p_{L}-p_{W}\bigr)
     =100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2\Delta_{c} .
\tag{1}
$$

The team which is first to empty is on the winning side.  With
$\max W<\max L$ the only essentially different finishing orders up to
renaming are

$$
W=\{1,3\},\,L=\{2,4\}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad W=\{1,4\},\,L=\{2,3\},
$$

and on $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$

$$
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,
$$

i.e. the four going out premiums cancel on the two teams.  The
$100_{W}$ win premium and the card swing are the only things that can
move in (1).  Put $p_{W}=0$, $p_{L}=P_{\max }$.  A point free 28 card
hand for the team which is first to empty and the whole $5$–$10$–$K$
stock in the other hand can be dealt, $\Delta_{c}^{\max}=P_{\max}$,
and (1) becomes

$$
X-Y\le 100_{W}+2P_{\max}
$$

signed.  In earned point book keeping the winner can therefore show

$$
X_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\qquad 
Y_{\rm earn}=0,
$$

the familiar $100$ for the win and $P_{\max}$ for the cards.

On the textbook $P_{\max}=100$ idealisation

$$
X-Y_{\rm signed}\le 100+2\times100=300,
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=100+P_{\max}=200$ for the winner and
$Y_{\rm signed}=-200$ for the loser, $X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=200$,
the $100$ point win plus a $100$ point net card advantage.  On the
real $1$–$10$–Mahjong normalisation $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10=52$
and with the Mahjong counted in the stock $P_{\max}=69$,

$$
X-Y_{\rm signed}\le 100+2\times69=238,\qquad
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,
$$

$100+2\times125=350$ signed, $225$ earned, with the $125$ point stock
including the $25$ point Mahjong.  This is the card $+$ win $+$ finishing
core forced by the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ restriction; the $+100/+100/-100/-100$
finishing account is killed by $\max W<\max L$.

Remark.  If the independent declaratory bonuses are kept in the
book keeping the ceiling is lifted by the Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong
and Dog premiums.  On the usual once per team normalisation the
earned ceiling under the same finishing restriction is
$P_{\max}+100_{W}+200_{Grand}+25_{M}=425$ for the winner and the
signed extremum is $X-Y\le535$, $625$ earned and $X-Y\le935$ signed
with the conventional two Grand Tichu calls per team.  The $100+2P_{\max}$
figure above is the part of that full ceiling which is forced by the
no $1$–$2$ finishing hypothesis.

3.text:
In the zero sum book keeping which is normally used for a round put

$S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L},$

$S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0$, $p_{L}$ the point stock which is still in the
hands of the losing team when the first team empties and
$p_{W}+p_{L}\le P_{\rm tot}$.  On the $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,
g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$ finishing table and with the first player out on
the winning side

${\rm max}\,W<{\rm max}\,L$

is, up to renaming,

$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$  or  $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$,

and in both cases

$S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,
\tag{1}$

i.e. the four individual finishing premiums cancel between the two
teams under the “the winners are not $1\!-\!2$’’ hypothesis.  Hence on the
signed zero sum sheet

$$
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}=100_{W}+2p_{L},
\tag{2}
$$

the only material left being the $100$ point round win and the card
swing.  With $p_{W}=0$ the winning team can be dealt a point free 28
card hand and the whole point stock can be put into the losing team.
On the textbook idealisation $P_{\rm tot}=100$

$$
p_{L}^{\max}=P_{\rm tot}=100,\qquad p_{W}^{\min}=0,
$$

so that in signed notation

$$
X-Y\le 100+2P_{\rm tot}=100+200=300
$$

points, i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=100+P_{\rm tot}=200$ for the winner and
$Y_{\rm signed}=-200$ for the loser.  In the ordinary earned point
book keeping which is written down on the score sheet this is the
familiar

$$
X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\rm tot}=200
$$

points, $100$ for the win and $100$ net card advantage, the finishing
account being neutral by (1).

On the real $1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock
$P_{\rm tot}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$ the signed ceiling is

$$
X-Y\le 100+2\times69=238,
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169$ points net on the winner’s sheet, $200$
points net on the $P_{\rm tot}=100$ idealisation.  With the Mahjong
counted in the point stock $P_{\rm tot}=125$ this is $X-Y\le350$
signed, $225$ earned.

*Remark.*  This is the card$+$win$+$finishing core which is forced by
${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$.  If the independent Tichu/Grand Tichu,
Mahjong and Dog bonuses are kept in the book keeping the ceiling is
lifted by the declaratory bonuses.  With the usual one call per team
normalisation and the finishing cancellation (1)

$$
X_{\max}=P_{\rm tot}+100_{W}+200_{Grand}+25_{M}=425
$$

net for the winner, $Y_{\min}=-110$ signed, i.e. $X-Y\le535$ signed.
With the conventional two Grand calls per team the textbook statement
is

$$
X_{\max}=P_{\rm tot}+100_{W}+2\times200_{Grand}+25_{M}=625,
$$

winner net, and in signed zero sum notation $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=625+310
=935$ points, $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm Grand}+25_{M}$ on the
winner and the mirror Dog/failed Grand penalties on the loser, the
$300$ signed/$200$ net card$+$win core above being the part of it which
is forced by the no $\{1,2\}$ finishing restriction.  This is the
$625$ line which is normally quoted for the full standard Tichu round.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The finishing cancellation is the key point and Colleague 4 has it right.

On the +100,+100,-100,-100 finishing scale the hypothesis “the winning team is not {1,2}” forces max W < max L. Up to renaming the only admissible orders with the first player out on the winning side are

W = {1,3}, L = {2,4}   or   W = {1,4}, L = {2,3},

and in both cases

S_W^p = +100-100 = 0,   S_L^p = 0,

so the four finishing bonuses cancel team-wise. Going-out therefore contributes nothing to the team swing under the stated restriction. That kills the first-out bonus that Colleague 6 wants to keep on the winning side and it is why the pure card+win core is 100+2P_max.

Cards. The 5-10-K stock is 100 points and the Mahjong can be put on the winning side. The point-free 28-card hand is dealable, so the maximal net card advantage that can be put on the winner is

Δc = P_max = 100  pip,   Δc_M = 125 with Mahjong.

In signed zero-sum bookkeeping a 100 pip swing is a 200 point signed card swing, 250 signed with Mahjong.

Tichu. The winner can make both of its calls Grand and succeed, 2×200 = 400. A maximal-difference construction does not require us to assume the losing team voluntarily calls Grand and fails. The loser can simply not call, or call and succeed on its own terms. The 800-point Tichu swing that underlies the 800/935 figures is obtained only by forcing two failed Grand calls on the loser, i.e. by assuming the loser self-harms. With the rational-play reading the Tichu contribution to the swing is the 400 points that can be put on the winning side, not 400+400.

Putting the attainable pieces together on the signed sheet that is normally quoted:

* round win  +100
* card / Mahjong   +100 pip +25 Mahjong
* finishing        0 under W≠{1,2}
* Tichu            +400 from two successful Grand calls

Hence the winner can be shown

X_max ≈ 100_win + 100_card + 25_M + 400_Grand = 625

in earned points, 100+100+400+25. With the Dog kept in the signed bookkeeping the loser is the one who receives the Dog in the W={1,3} or W={1,4} realisations, i.e. -10 on Y, giving a signed swing of 635.

That is the material that is actually realisable under the “winner is not 1-2’’ restriction. The 300/238 card+win core of C1/C2/C5 is the same result with Tichu stripped out; the 935 signed / 535 one-call figures of C3 are the 625 core plus the extra assumption that the loser is forced to make and fail two Grand calls and that Mahjong/Dog are double counted inside the 125-point stock.

The 800-point claim needs both a non-zero going-out net and the 400-point loser Tichu failure. Once going-out is correctly cancelled to zero and the loser is not assumed to self-damage, the coherent high end of the round under the stated restriction is the 100+100+400+25 ≈ 625 point winner ceiling, 635 signed with Dog, i.e. the 625/635 family that Colleague 4 isolates.

public_text.6:
The card+win+finishing core that everybody is agreeing on is the right starting point, and it is the part that is forced by the “winner is not {1,2}” hypothesis.

On the usual signed zero-sum sheet the four finishing bonuses cancel per team under max W < max L.  Up to renaming the only essentially different orders are W={1,3},L={2,4} and W={1,4},L={2,3}.  In both cases S_W^p = +100-100 =0 and S_L^p =0, so the finishing account is neutral per team.  The hypothesis does not forbid the winning team from taking first place, it only forbids W={1,2}.  Hence the winner can keep the first-out +100 while the loser takes second-out +100, i.e. the first-out premium stays on the winning side of the hand.  That is why the pure cancellation argument for the going-out account is too strong.

Once the finishing account is neutralised the only things that can move the signed swing are the round win premium and the declaratory premiums.  On the cards the textbook extremum is attainable in the deal: the winning team can be dealt a point-free 28-card hand and take the whole 5-10-K stock, 100 points net, 200 points in signed notation.  The 25 point Mahjong is an independent bonus and it can be put on the winning side.

The Tichu premiums are part of the standard round score and they are independent of the card/ finishing core.  Each player is allowed one call per round.  The maximal call is Grand Tichu, +200 signed for success and –200 signed for failure.  For a maximal-difference bound we are entitled to put the whole declaratory premium on the winning side: the winning team makes two Grand calls and both succeed, +400 signed; the losing team makes two Grand calls and both fail, –400 signed.  That is a 800 point signed swing from the two teams’ Tichu premiums alone, and it is the normal way the maximal bound is quoted.

Putting the independent pieces together in the signed convention that is normally used for X-Y:

* net card differential 100 points, 200 points signed;
* round win swing 100 to winner, –100 to loser, 200 points signed;
* first-out can stay with the winner under W={1,3}, +100 on the winning side, –100 on the losing side in the symmetric book-keeping;
* 2×Grand Tichu success +400 to winner, 2×Grand Tichu failure –400 to loser.

In per-team net language that is the familiar 100 pip differential +100 first-out +200 per Grand =400 points net for the winning team, and the mirror –400 for the losing team in signed book-keeping.  Signed X-Y is therefore

X-Y = 400 – (–400) = 800 points,

i.e. an unsigned winner ceiling of about 100 cards +25 Mahjong +100 win +400 Grand =625 points, the 625 figure Colleague 4 quotes, and 800 points signed once the loser’s mirror is written down.

The 238/300/0 family is the card-only textbook ceiling and it is correct only if Tichu/Grand Tichu are stripped out.  The 935 figure over-counts: it adds Mahjong and Dog on top of an already maximal 125 point stock, treats Dog as an extra –10 on top of the signed finishing cancellation and double counts the Mahjong inside the point stock.  Once those double counts are removed the coherent high end under the non-first-and-second restriction is the 800 signed swing, 625 unsigned winner score, which is the card+win+first-out+Grand ceiling that is normally quoted in the literature. ∎

$$

$$

$$

signed.  In earned book keeping the winner can show

$$

$$

signed card swing.  This is the $100+2P_{\max}$ card-plus-win ceiling

neutral under the restriction.

4\cdot10+25=69$ the signed ceiling is $100+2\times69=238$, $169$

300$ signed, $200$ net on the conventional $100$-point idealisation.

$$

points and the loser $0$ points, the familiar $100+P_{\max}$ net
ceiling.  In signed notation this is the quoted

$200$ points net on the winner's sheet, $100$ points for the win and

The finishing cancellation is the key point and Colleague 4 has it right.

On the +100,+100,-100,-100 finishing scale the hypothesis “the winning team is not {1,2}” forces max W < max L. Up to renaming the only admissible orders with the first player out on the winning side are

W = {1,3}, L = {2,4}   or   W = {1,4}, L = {2,3},

and in both cases

S_W^p = +100-100 = 0,   S_L^p = 0,

so the four finishing bonuses cancel team-wise. Going-out therefore contributes nothing to the team swing under the stated restriction. That kills the first-out bonus that Colleague 6 wants to keep on the winning side and it is why the pure card+win core is 100+2P_max.

Cards. The 5-10-K stock is 100 points and the Mahjong can be put on the winning side. The point-free 28-card hand is dealable, so the maximal net card advantage that can be put on the winner is

Δc = P_max = 100  pip,   Δc_M = 125 with Mahjong.

In signed zero-sum bookkeeping a 100 pip swing is a 200 point signed card swing, 250 signed with Mahjong.

Tichu. The winner can make both of its calls Grand and succeed, 2×200 = 400. A maximal-difference construction does not require us to assume the losing team voluntarily calls Grand and fails. The loser can simply not call, or call and succeed on its own terms. The 800-point Tichu swing that underlies the 800/935 figures is obtained only by forcing two failed Grand calls on the loser, i.e. by assuming the loser self-harms. With the rational-play reading the Tichu contribution to the swing is the 400 points that can be put on the winning side, not 400+400.

Putting the attainable pieces together on the signed sheet that is normally quoted:

* round win  +100
* card / Mahjong   +100 pip +25 Mahjong
* finishing        0 under W≠{1,2}
* Tichu            +400 from two successful Grand calls

Hence the winner can be shown

X_max ≈ 100_win + 100_card + 25_M + 400_Grand = 625

in earned points, 100+100+400+25. With the Dog kept in the signed bookkeeping the loser is the one who receives the Dog in the W={1,3} or W={1,4} realisations, i.e. -10 on Y, giving a signed swing of 635.

That is the material that is actually realisable under the “winner is not 1-2’’ restriction. The 300/238 card+win core of C1/C2/C5 is the same result with Tichu stripped out; the 935 signed / 535 one-call figures of C3 are the 625 core plus the extra assumption that the loser is forced to make and fail two Grand calls and that Mahjong/Dog are double counted inside the 125-point stock.

The 800-point claim needs both a non-zero going-out net and the 400-point loser Tichu failure. Once going-out is correctly cancelled to zero and the loser is not assumed to self-damage, the coherent high end of the round under the stated restriction is the 100+100+400+25 ≈ 625 point winner ceiling, 635 signed with Dog, i.e. the 625/635 family that Colleague 4 isolates.

Y_min ≈ C_L+100_go-out-10_Dog-Tichu_failure

Under the max W<max L restriction the going-out premiums cancel per team, so the 100_go-out term is neutral on the swing. With C_W=100, C_L=0, two Grand Tichu calls per team succeed for winner and fail for loser, Mahjong to winner, Dog to loser:

Y_min ≈ C_L+100_go-out-10_Dog-Tichu_failure

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with Colleague 4 on the finishing cancellation being the decisive point under the hypothesis as it is normally read in this set-up.

On the ±100,±100 finishing table put $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$ and $S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}$, $S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}}$. With the first player out on the winning side the condition “the winning team is not {1,2}’’ is ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$. Up to renaming the admissible orders are

$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ or $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$

and in both

$S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,$

so the four individual going-out premiums cancel teamwise. That is why the card+win+finishing core is $100_{win}+2P_{\max}$ signed, $100_{win}+P_{\max}$ earned, the $300$ signed / $200$ net figure of C1/C2/C3. The finishing account is neutral; the first-out premium cannot be kept on the winner in addition to the neutralisation.

Cards. A point-free 28-card hand for the first emptying team is dealable. On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$ pip, $125$ pip with the Mahjong in the stock, so the net card advantage that can be put on the winner is $\Delta_{c}=100$, $125$ with Mahjong. In signed bookkeeping that is $200$ points signed, $250$ signed with Mahjong.

Tichu is independent of the card/finishing core. The maximal attainable declaratory contribution to the swing is the $+400$ that can be put on the winning side by two successful Grand Tichu calls, $2\times200$. A maximal-difference construction does not require us to assume the losing team voluntarily calls Grand and fails. The $800$-point Tichu swing used for the $800$ signed / $935$ signed figures is obtained only by forcing two failed Grand calls on the loser, i.e. by assuming the loser self-harms. With the rational-play reading the Tichu contribution to the attainable swing is the $400$ points that can be put on the winning side, not $400+400$.

Putting the attainable pieces together on the signed sheet normally quoted:

* round win $+100$
* card / Mahjong $+100$ pip $+25$ Mahjong
* finishing $0$ under $W\neq\{1,2\}$
* Tichu $+400$ from two successful Grand calls

Hence in earned points

$X_{\max}\approx100_{win}+100_{card}+25_{M}+400_{Grand}=625$

and with the Dog kept in the signed bookkeeping the loser is the one who receives the Dog in the $W=\{1,3\}$ or $W=\{1,4\}$ realisations, giving a signed swing of $\approx635$. That is the $100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}$ family Colleague 4 isolates.

The $800$ signed claim of Colleague 6 needs both a non-zero going-out net and the $400$-point loser Tichu failure. Once going-out is correctly cancelled to $0$ under ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and the loser is not assumed to self-damage, the coherent high end is the $625$ earned / $\sim635$ signed family. The $935$ signed / $535$ one-call figures of C3 are the $625$ core plus the extra assumption that the loser is forced to make and fail two Grand calls and that Mahjong/Dog are double counted inside the $125$-point stock. The card+win $300$ signed / $238$ real core of C1/C2/C5 is the same result with Tichu stripped out.

$$
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}},\qquad S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}},\qquad
S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0 .
$$
With $p_{L}$ for the point stock which is still in the hands of the
losing team when the first team empties

$$
S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L}
$$

in the signed zero sum convention, so that

$$
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L} .
\tag{1}
$$

The first player out is always on the winning side.  With the
hypothesis ``the winning team is not $\{1,2\}$'' we have ${\rm max}W<
{\rm max}L$ and, up to renaming,

$$
W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}\quad{\rm or}\quad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\},
$$

and on the $\pm100$ table

$$
S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,
$$

i.e. the four individual going out premiums cancel team-wise.  Hence
(1) becomes

$$
X-Y=100_{W}+2p_{L},\qquad p_{L}\le P_{\max},\;p_{W}\ge0,
$$

the hand win and the card swing being the only material left.  The
28-card hand which is first to empty can be made point free and the
whole point stock can be put into the opponents.  On the textbook
$5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ idealisation

$$
P_{\max}=4\times5+4\times10+4\times10=100 ,
$$

so that with $p_{W}=0,\;p_{L}=P_{\max}$ in signed zero-sum bookkeeping

$$
S_{W}=100+P_{\max}=200,\qquad S_{L}=-100-P_{\max}=-200,
$$

i.e.

$$
X-Y\le 100+2P_{\max}=100+200=300
$$

signed, $100$ for the hand win and $100$ net card advantage.  In the
ordinary earned-point book keeping written on the score sheet this is

$$
X_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max}=200,\qquad Y_{\rm earn}=0,
$$

the familiar $100+ P_{\max}$ net ceiling.  The $+100/+100/-100/-100$
finishing contribution is killed by $W\ne\{1,2\}$, $S_{W}^{p}=0$, so the
$300$ signed/$200$ net figure is the card+win+finishing core forced by
the no-$\{1,2\}$ restriction.

On the real $1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock $P_{\max}=4\!\cdot\!1+
4\!\cdot\!10+25=69$, i.e. $52$ points of $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$, the signed
ceiling is

$$
X-Y\le 100+2\times69=238\ {\rm signed},
$$

$X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169$, $225$ earned, $350$ signed with the
Mahjong counted in the stock $P_{\max}=125$.  This is the
$100+2P_{\max}$ card-plus-win core on which the full declaratory
book keeping is built.  With the usual independent Tichu/Grand-Tichu,
Mahjong and Dog premiums kept on top of the core one obtains the
customary full-rule numbers $X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+200_{Grand}+25_{M}
=425$ earned, $X-Y\le535$ signed on a one-call-per-team normalisation,
and $X_{\max}=625$ earned, $X-Y\le935$ signed on the conventional
two-Grand-call-per-team normalisation.  The $300$ signed/$200$ net
card+win+finishing bound above is the part of it which is forced by
$\max W<\max L$, i.e. by the winning team not being $\{1,2\}$. ∎

3.text:
On the signed zero sum sheet write $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$
and put $S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}},~S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}}$.
Put $p_{W},p_{L}$ for the point cards which are still in the hands of the
two teams when the hand closes and $p_{W}+p_{L}=P$.  On the ordinary
$+100$ round win

$$
S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L},
\qquad S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0 ,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2
\Delta_{c},\qquad \Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W}.
\end{equation*}
The team which is first to empty is on the winning side.  With the
hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$ we have ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and up to
renaming

$$
W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}\qquad {\rm or}\qquad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\},
$$

and on the $\pm100,\pm100$ finishing table

$$
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0 ,
$$

i.e. the four individual going out premiums cancel team-wise under the
no $\{1,2\}$ restriction.  Hence

$$
X-Y=100_{W}+2p_{L},
\tag{*}
$$

the only material left being the $100$ point round win and the card
swing.  The 28 cards of the first emptying team can be made point free
and the whole point stock can be put into the opponents.  On the
textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$ pip

$$
p_{W}^{\min}=0,\qquad p_{L}^{\max}=P_{\max},
$$

so that $(*)$ gives in signed zero sum notation

$$
X-Y\le 100+2P_{\max},\qquad 
X_{\rm signed}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\;Y_{\rm signed}=-100_{W}-P_{\max},
$$

i.e. $100$ points for the win and a $P_{\max}$ net card advantage.
In the earned point book keeping that is written down on the score
sheet

$$
X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},
$$

the familiar $100$ for the win and $P_{\max}$ net card advantage, the
finishing account being neutral by $S_{W}^{p}=0$.

On the textbook $100$ pip idealisation

$$
X-Y_{\max}=100+2\times100=300\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=200$, $Y_{\rm signed}=-200$ and
$X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the winner's
sheet, $100$ for the win and $100$ net card advantage.  On the real
$1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$,
$52$ pip without the Mahjong, the signed textbook bound forced by
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$$
X-Y\le100+2\times69=238\;{\rm signed},\qquad 
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,
$$

$100+2P_{\max}$ signed, $100+P_{\max}$ earned.  With the Mahjong
counted in the stock $P_{\max}=125$ this is $X-Y\le350$ signed,
$225$ earned.  This is the card$+$win$+$finishing core which is forced
by ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$; the $+100/+100/-100/-100$ finishing
contribution is killed by the hypothesis.

Remark.  The independent Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and Dog premiums
stack on top of the core.  On the conventional one-call-per-team
normalisation the earned ceiling under the same finishing cancellation is

$$
X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+200_{Grand}+25_{M},
$$

$425$ earned on the $P_{\max}=100$ idealisation and $535$ signed,
$Y_{\min}=100_{go\;out}-10_{Dog}-200_{Grand}=-110$.  With the
conventional two Grand calls per team this is the textbook
$X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}=625$ earned,
$Y_{\min}=100_{go\;out}-10_{Dog}-400_{Grand}=-310$, i.e. $X-Y\le
625+310=935$ signed, the $100_{card}+100_{win}-100_{go\;out}+
800_{Tichu}+25_{M}+10_{Dog}$ family.  The $100+2P_{\max}$ i.e. $300$
signed/$200$ earned figure above is the part of that ceiling which is
forced by the no $\{1,2\}$ finishing restriction and is independent of
the declaratory bonuses. ∎

5.text:
On the $\pm 100,\pm100$ going out table put
$g_{1}=+100,\;g_{2}=+100,\;g_{3}=-100,\;g_{4}=-100$ and
$S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}},\;S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}}$.  With the
ordinary hand win

\begin{equation*}
S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad 
S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L},\qquad S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0,
\end{equation*}
so that on the signed sheet

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}
      =100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2\Delta_{c},\qquad 
\Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W},
\end{equation*}
with $p_{W}+p_{L}\le P_{\rm tot}$.

The first team to empty is on the winning side.  With the hypothesis
$\max W<\max L$, i.e. $W\ne\{1,2\}$, up to renaming

\[
W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}\quad{\rm or}\quad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}\quad 
{\rm or}\quad W=\{2,3\},L=\{1,4\},
\]

and

\[
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,
\]

i.e. the four individual going–out premiums cancel teamwise under the
no $\{1,2\}$ restriction.  The only material left in (1) is the
$100$ point round win and the card swing.  Put $p_{W}=0$.  A point free
28 card hand for the first emptying team is dealable and the whole
$5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock can be put into the opponents, so that

\[
\Delta_{c}^{\max}=p_{L}^{\max}-0=P_{\max},
\]

and with $S_{W}^{p}=0$

\[
X-Y=100+2p_{L}\le 100+2P_{\max},\qquad 
X_{\rm signed}=100+P_{\max},\;Y_{\rm signed}=-100-P_{\max},
\]

on the signed zero-sum sheet.  In earned point book keeping this is

\[
X_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\qquad Y_{\rm earn}=0,
\]

the familiar $100$ for the win and $P_{\max}$ net card advantage, the
finishing account being neutral by $S_{W}^{p}=0$.

On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$

\[
X-Y_{\max}^{\rm signed}=100+2\times100=300,
\]

i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=200,\;Y_{\rm signed}=-200$, $X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm
earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the winner's sheet, $100$ points
for the win and $100$ points net card swing.  On the real
$1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10=52$ and
with the Mahjong counted in the stock $P_{\max}=69$,

\[
X-Y_{\max}^{\rm signed}=100+2\times69=238,\qquad
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,
\]

$100+2\times125=350$ signed, $225$ net, with the $125$ point stock
including the $25$ point Mahjong.  This is the card $+$ win $+$
finishing core which is forced by $\max W<\max L$; the
$+100/+100/-100/-100$ finishing contribution is killed by the
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis.

Remark on the declaratory bonuses.  Once Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and
Dog are kept the ceiling is lifted by the independent declaratory
premia.  With the conventional two Grand calls per team the textbook
quoted extremum is

\[
X_{\max}^{\rm earn}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+400_{\rm Grand}+25_{M}=625,
\]

winner net, and in signed zero sum notation
$Y_{\min}=100_{\rm go\;out}-10_{\rm Dog}-400_{\rm Grand}=-310$, i.e.

\[
X-Y\le625+310=935\;{\rm signed},\qquad
100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm go\;out}+800_{\rm Tichu}
+25_{M}+10_{\rm Dog},
\]

the $300$ signed/$200$ net card$+$win core above being the part of it
which is forced by the no $\{1,2\}$ finishing restriction.  With the
one-call-per-team normalisation this is the familiar
$X_{\max}=425$ earned, $X-Y\le535$ signed family.  The $100+2P_{\max}$
core is the material that is inescapable under $W\ne\{1,2\}$; the
$625/935$ numbers are the usual full-rule maximal-difference quotes
built on top of it. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The card-plus-win-plus-finishing core is the part that is forced by “the winning team is not {1,2}’’ and everyone now agrees on it.

On the ±100,±100 finishing table with the first player out on the winning side the only orders compatible with max W < max L up to renaming are

W = {1,3}, L = {2,4}  and  W = {1,4}, L = {2,3},

and in both cases S_W^p = +100-100 =0, S_L^p =0 per team. That is a team-wise cancellation, not a hand-wise disappearance of the first-out premium. The hypothesis forbids W={1,2} it does not forbid the winning side taking first place. With W={1,3} the winner keeps the first-out +100 and the loser keeps the second-out +100, so the finishing account is neutral per team but the signed swing still contains the first-out premium on the winning side of the hand. That is why the pure 100+2P_max card+win core is the minimum, not the maximum.

Once the finishing account is neutralised per team the independent pieces can be stacked.

Cards. The 28-card hand that empties first can be made point free and the whole 5-10-K stock can be put into the opponents. On the textbook idealisation P_max=100 pip, 200 points signed. The 25-point Mahjong is an independent declaratory bonus and can be put on the winning side.

Win. The round win is +100 to the winner, –100 to the loser in signed bookkeeping, 200 points signed swing.

Tichu. Each player is allowed one call per round. The maximal call is Grand Tichu, +200 signed for success, –200 signed for failure. For a maximal-difference bound we are entitled to put the whole declaratory premium on the winning side. The winning team makes two Grand calls and both succeed, +400 signed. The losing team can be made to make two Grand calls and both fail, –400 signed. That is the normal way the maximal bound is quoted and it is not an “unreasonable self-harm’’ assumption, it is the extremal realisation of the declaratory game.

Putting the attainable pieces together in the signed convention that is normally used for X-Y:

* net card differential 100 pip, 200 points signed;
* round win swing 100 to winner, –100 to loser;
* first-out can stay with the winner under W={1,3}, +100 on the winning side in the signed account;
* 2×Grand Tichu success +400 to winner, 2×Grand Tichu failure –400 to loser.

In per-team net language that is the familiar 100 pip differential +100 first-out +25 Mahjong +100 win +400 Grand =625 points on the winner’s sheet, the 625 unsigned ceiling that Colleague 4 isolates. In signed zero-sum bookkeeping the mirror is written on the loser, giving

X-Y = 400 – (–400) =800 points signed,

i.e. an unsigned winner ceiling of about 100 cards +25 Mahjong +100 win +100 first-out +400 Grand =725 points, usually quoted as the 625 unsigned /800 signed family with the first-out absorbed in the signed cancellation.

The 238/300/0 family is correct only if Tichu/Grand Tichu is stripped out. The 935 signed claim of C3 over-counts: it adds Mahjong and Dog on top of an already maximal 125-point stock, treats Dog as an extra –10 on top of the signed finishing cancellation and double counts Mahjong inside the point stock. Once those double counts are removed and the loser’s Grand failures are kept as part of the extremal declaratory swing, the coherent high end under the non-first-and-second restriction is the 800 signed swing, 625 unsigned winner score, which is the card+win+first-out+Grand ceiling normally quoted in the literature.

On the ±100,±100 finishing table put $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$ and $S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}$, $S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}}$. $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ or $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$

and in both

$S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,$

so the four individual going-out premiums cancel teamwise. That is why the card+win+finishing core is $100_{win}+2P_{\max}$ signed, $100_{win}+P_{\max}$ earned, the $300$ signed / $200$ net figure of C1/C2/C3. The finishing account is neutral; the first-out premium cannot be kept on the winner in addition to the neutralisation.

On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$ pip, $125$ pip with the Mahjong in the stock, so the net card advantage that can be put on the winner is $\Delta_{c}=100$, $125$ with Mahjong. In signed bookkeeping that is $200$ points signed, $250$ signed with Mahjong.

Tichu is independent of the card/finishing core. The maximal attainable declaratory contribution to the swing is the $+400$ that can be put on the winning side by two successful Grand Tichu calls, $2\times200$. A maximal-difference construction does not require us to assume the losing team voluntarily calls Grand and fails. The $800$-point Tichu swing used for the $800$ signed / $935$ signed figures is obtained only by forcing two failed Grand calls on the loser, i.e. by assuming the loser self-harms. With the rational-play reading the Tichu contribution to the attainable swing is the $400$ points that can be put on the winning side, not $400+400$.

Putting the attainable pieces together on the signed sheet normally quoted:

* round win $+100$
* card / Mahjong $+100$ pip $+25$ Mahjong
* finishing $0$ under $W\neq\{1,2\}$
* Tichu $+400$ from two successful Grand calls

Hence in earned points

$X_{\max}\approx100_{win}+100_{card}+25_{M}+400_{Grand}=625$

and with the Dog kept in the signed bookkeeping the loser is the one who receives the Dog in the $W=\{1,3\}$ or $W=\{1,4\}$ realisations, giving a signed swing of $\approx635$. That is the $100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}$ family Colleague 4 isolates.

The $800$ signed claim of Colleague 6 needs both a non-zero going-out net and the $400$-point loser Tichu failure. Once going-out is correctly cancelled to $0$ under ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and the loser is not assumed to self-damage, the coherent high end is the $625$ earned / $\sim635$ signed family. The $935$ signed / $535$ one-call figures of C3 are the $625$ core plus the extra assumption that the loser is forced to make and fail two Grand calls and that Mahjong/Dog are double counted inside the $125$-point stock. The card+win $300$ signed / $238$ real core of C1/C2/C5 is the same result with Tichu stripped out.

The team which is first to empty is on the winning side.  With the
hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$ we have ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and up to
renaming

$$
W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}\qquad {\rm or}\qquad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\},
$$

and on the $\pm100,\pm100$ finishing table

$$
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0 ,
$$

i.e. the four individual going out premiums cancel team-wise under the
no $\{1,2\}$ restriction.  Hence

$$
X-Y=100_{W}+2p_{L},
\tag{*}
$$

the only material left being the $100$ point round win and the card
swing.  The 28 cards of the first emptying team can be made point free
and the whole point stock can be put into the opponents.  On the
textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$ pip

$$
p_{W}^{\min}=0,\qquad p_{L}^{\max}=P_{\max},
$$

so that $(*)$ gives in signed zero sum notation

$$
X-Y\le 100+2P_{\max},\qquad 
X_{\rm signed}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\;Y_{\rm signed}=-100_{W}-P_{\max},
$$

i.e. $100$ points for the win and a $P_{\max}$ net card advantage.
In the earned point book keeping that is written down on the score
sheet

$$
X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},
$$

the familiar $100$ for the win and $P_{\max}$ net card advantage, the
finishing account being neutral by $S_{W}^{p}=0$.

On the textbook $100$ pip idealisation

$$
X-Y_{\max}=100+2\times100=300\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=200$, $Y_{\rm signed}=-200$ and
$X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the winner's
sheet, $100$ for the win and $100$ net card advantage.  On the real
$1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ stock $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$,
$52$ pip without the Mahjong, the signed textbook bound forced by
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is

$$
X-Y\le100+2\times69=238\;{\rm signed},\qquad 
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,
$$

$100+2P_{\max}$ signed, $100+P_{\max}$ earned.  With the Mahjong
counted in the stock $P_{\max}=125$ this is $X-Y\le350$ signed,
$225$ earned.  This is the card$+$win$+$finishing core which is forced
by ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$; the $+100/+100/-100/-100$ finishing
contribution is killed by the hypothesis.

Remark.  The independent Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and Dog premiums
stack on top of the core.  On the conventional one-call-per-team
normalisation the earned ceiling under the same finishing cancellation is

$$
X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+200_{Grand}+25_{M},
$$

$425$ earned on the $P_{\max}=100$ idealisation and $535$ signed,
$Y_{\min}=100_{go\;out}-10_{Dog}-200_{Grand}=-110$.  With the
conventional two Grand calls per team this is the textbook
$X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}=625$ earned,
$Y_{\min}=100_{go\;out}-10_{Dog}-400_{Grand}=-310$, i.e. $X-Y\le
625+310=935$ signed, the $100_{card}+100_{win}-100_{go\;out}+
800_{Tichu}+25_{M}+10_{Dog}$ family.  The $100+2P_{\max}$ i.e. $300$
signed/$200$ earned figure above is the part of that ceiling which is
forced by the no $\{1,2\}$ finishing restriction and is independent of
the declaratory bonuses. ∎

\begin{equation*}

      =100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2\Delta_{c},\qquad

\end{equation*}
with $p_{W}+p_{L}\le P_{\rm tot}$.

\]

no $\{1,2\}$ restriction.  The only material left in (1) is the
$100$ point round win and the card swing.  Put $p_{W}=0$.  A point free
28 card hand for the first emptying team is dealable and the whole
$5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock can be put into the opponents, so that

\[
\Delta_{c}^{\max}=p_{L}^{\max}-0=P_{\max},
\]

and with $S_{W}^{p}=0$

\]

on the signed zero-sum sheet.  In earned point book keeping this is

\[
X_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\qquad Y_{\rm earn}=0,
\]

the familiar $100$ for the win and $P_{\max}$ net card advantage, the
finishing account being neutral by $S_{W}^{p}=0$.

On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$

\[
X-Y_{\max}^{\rm signed}=100+2\times100=300,
\]

i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=200,\;Y_{\rm signed}=-200$, $X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm
earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the winner's sheet, $100$ points

\[
X-Y_{\max}^{\rm signed}=100+2\times69=238,\qquad
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,
\]

finishing core which is forced by $\max W<\max L$; the
$+100/+100/-100/-100$ finishing contribution is killed by the

Remark on the declaratory bonuses.  Once Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and
Dog are kept the ceiling is lifted by the independent declaratory

\[

\]

\]

public_text.6:
The card-plus-win-plus-finishing core is the part that is forced by “the winning team is not {1,2}’’ and everyone now agrees on it.

On the ±100,±100 finishing table with the first player out on the winning side the only orders compatible with max W < max L up to renaming are

W = {1,3}, L = {2,4}  and  W = {1,4}, L = {2,3},

and in both cases S_W^p = +100-100 =0, S_L^p =0 per team. That is a team-wise cancellation, not a hand-wise disappearance of the first-out premium. The hypothesis forbids W={1,2} it does not forbid the winning side taking first place. With W={1,3} the winner keeps the first-out +100 and the loser keeps the second-out +100, so the finishing account is neutral per team but the signed swing still contains the first-out premium on the winning side of the hand. That is why the pure 100+2P_max card+win core is the minimum, not the maximum.

Once the finishing account is neutralised per team the independent pieces can be stacked.

Cards. The 28-card hand that empties first can be made point free and the whole 5-10-K stock can be put into the opponents. On the textbook idealisation P_max=100 pip, 200 points signed. The 25-point Mahjong is an independent declaratory bonus and can be put on the winning side.

Win. The round win is +100 to the winner, –100 to the loser in signed bookkeeping, 200 points signed swing.

Tichu. Each player is allowed one call per round. The maximal call is Grand Tichu, +200 signed for success, –200 signed for failure. For a maximal-difference bound we are entitled to put the whole declaratory premium on the winning side. The winning team makes two Grand calls and both succeed, +400 signed. The losing team can be made to make two Grand calls and both fail, –400 signed. That is the normal way the maximal bound is quoted and it is not an “unreasonable self-harm’’ assumption, it is the extremal realisation of the declaratory game.

Putting the attainable pieces together in the signed convention that is normally used for X-Y:

* net card differential 100 pip, 200 points signed;
* round win swing 100 to winner, –100 to loser;
* first-out can stay with the winner under W={1,3}, +100 on the winning side in the signed account;
* 2×Grand Tichu success +400 to winner, 2×Grand Tichu failure –400 to loser.

In per-team net language that is the familiar 100 pip differential +100 first-out +25 Mahjong +100 win +400 Grand =625 points on the winner’s sheet, the 625 unsigned ceiling that Colleague 4 isolates. In signed zero-sum bookkeeping the mirror is written on the loser, giving

X-Y = 400 – (–400) =800 points signed,

i.e. an unsigned winner ceiling of about 100 cards +25 Mahjong +100 win +100 first-out +400 Grand =725 points, usually quoted as the 625 unsigned /800 signed family with the first-out absorbed in the signed cancellation.

The 238/300/0 family is correct only if Tichu/Grand Tichu is stripped out. The 935 signed claim of C3 over-counts: it adds Mahjong and Dog on top of an already maximal 125-point stock, treats Dog as an extra –10 on top of the signed finishing cancellation and double counts Mahjong inside the point stock. Once those double counts are removed and the loser’s Grand failures are kept as part of the extremal declaratory swing, the coherent high end under the non-first-and-second restriction is the 800 signed swing, 625 unsigned winner score, which is the card+win+first-out+Grand ceiling normally quoted in the literature.

With the usual $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$ finishing
table put

$S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L},\qquad
S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0 ,$

$p_{L}$ being the point points which are still in the hands of the loser
when the first team empties.  On signed zero sum

$X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}\;, $

and $\Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W}$.  The first emptying player is on the
winning side.  With the hypothesis

${\rm max}\,W<{\rm max}\,L$,

i.e. the winning team is not $\{1,2\}$, up to renaming

$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ or $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$,

and on the $\pm100,\pm100$ table

$S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0$,

so that the four going-out premiums cancel teamwise under the
no-$\{1,2\}$ restriction.  Hence

$X-Y =100_{W}+2p_{L}=100_{W}+2\Delta_{c}\;, $

the only material left being the $100$ point round premium and the card
swing.  Put $p_{W}=0$.  A point free 28 card hand for the first emptying
team can be dealt and the whole point stock can be put into the other
team.  On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$

$p_{L}^{\max}=P_{\max},\qquad\Delta_{c}^{\max}=P_{\max}$,

so that on the signed sheet

$X-Y\le 100+2P_{\max}\;,$

i.e.

$X_{\rm signed}=100+P_{\max},\qquad 
Y_{\rm signed}=-(100+P_{\max}),$

and in earned point book keeping

$X_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\qquad Y_{\rm earn}=0,$

the familiar $100$ for the win and $P_{\max}$ net card advantage.  With
the textbook $P_{\max}=100$

$X-Y_{\max}=100+2\times100=300\;{\rm signed},$

$X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the winner's
sheet, $100$ for the win and $100$ net card advantage, the finishing
account being neutral by $S_{W}^{p}=0$.  On the real $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$
stock $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10=52$ and with the Mahjong in the stock
$P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$,

$X-Y\le100+2\times69=238\;{\rm signed},\qquad
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,$

$350$ signed, $225$ earned, with the $125$ point idealisation
$P_{\max}=125$.  This is the card$+$win$+$finishing core which is forced
by $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

Remark.  The declaratory premiums are independent of the core.  With the
usual two Grand Tichu calls per team, Mahjong $+25$ and Dog $-10$ the
earned ceiling under the same finishing cancellation is

$X_{\max}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}=625$

on the textbook $P_{\max}=100$ idealisation, $569$ on the real $69$
point stock, and in signed zero sum notation $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=935$
signed, $100_{card}+100_{win}-100_{go out}+800_{Tichu}+25_{M}+10_{Dog}$,
the $300$ signed/$200$ net figure above being the $100_{W}+2P_{\max}$

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The finishing algebra is now stable across rounds.
On the ±100,±100 finishing table with the first emptying player on the winning side the hypothesis “winning team does not go out first and second’’ is max W < max L. Up to renaming the admissible orders are W={1,3},L={2,4} or W={1,4},L={2,3} – W={2,3},L={1,4} is allowed only if first out need not be on W. In all admissible orders S_W^p = g_W1+g_W2 = +100-100 =0 and S_L^p=0, so the four going-out premiums cancel team-wise.

With signed zero-sum bookkeeping
S_W =100_W+ S_W^p + p_L ,  S_L = S_L^p - p_L ,  S_W^p+S_L^p=0
X-Y =100_W+2 S_W^p+2 p_L =100_W+2 p_L =100_W+2 Δ_c , Δ_c = p_L-p_W .
The card+win+finishing core is therefore forced by  W≠{1,2}.

Card extremum. A point-free 28-card hand for the first emptying team is dealable.
Textbook idealisation P_max =100 pip points can be put entirely in the loser’s hands, Δ_c^max =100. Real 1-10-Mahjong stock is P_max =4·1+4·10+25=69 for 5-10-K+Mahjong, 52 pip only.
Hence signed core
X-Y ≤100+2P_max =300 signed ideal, 238 signed real 69,
earned core X_earn-Y_earn =100+P_max =200 ideal, 169 real.
With Mahjong counted in the stock P_max=125 gives 350 signed /225 earned.

Declaratory bonuses are independent of the core.
Standard suite: Tichu +100 / Grand Tichu +200, Mahjong +25, Dog –10, round win +100.
With two successful Grand calls per winning team and two failed Grand calls per losing team, Mahjong to winner, Dog to loser, the earned ceiling under the same finishing cancellation is
X_max = P_max+100_W+400_Grand+25_M =625 earned on P_max=100 ideal, 569 on P_max=69 real,
Y_min =100_go out –10_Dog –400_Grand = –310,
signed swing X_max – Y_min =625+310 =935 signed,
i.e. 100_card+100_win–100_go out+800_Tichu+25_M+10_Dog.
One-call-per-team normalisation is the familiar
X_max =P_max+100+200+25 =425 earned, Y_min =100-10-200=–110, X-Y ≤535 signed.

The disagreement in round 3 is about how much of that stack is “maximal possible’’ vs “guaranteeable’’.

Colleague 4 rational-play reading: the loser need not voluntarily call and fail Grand; the 800-point Tichu swing then reduces to the +400 points that can be put on the winner. With S_W^p=0 the first-out +100 is already absorbed in the +100–100 cancellation, so the coherent high end is the 625 earned / ~635 signed family, X_max≈100_win+100_card+25_M+400_Grand.

Colleague 6 keeps the mirror failure and argues first-out can stay with the winner under W={1,3}. It treats the per-team neutralisation as not removing the first-out premium from the signed swing, leading to the 800 signed swing i.e. an unsigned winner ceiling ≈100_card+25_M+100_win+100_first-out+400_Grand≈725, usually quoted as 625 unsigned /800 signed. The 935 signed claim is then said to over-count Mahjong/Dog inside the 125-point stock.

Unresolved:
* signed zero-sum X-Y vs earned X_earn–Y_earn bookkeeping;
* whether Mahjong is counted inside P_max or as an independent +25;
* whether the maximal bound should assume the loser voluntarily fails two Grands and takes the Dog, as is normal for extremal deals, or should restrict to premiums the winner can guarantee;
* exact Dog/Mahjong allocation under W={1,3}/{1,4} and the 100/100/–100/–100 vs 100/50/–50/–100 finishing table;
* whether first out must be on the winning side, which eliminates W={2,3},L={1,4}.

Current best synthesis: finishing cancels under max W < max L. The forced card+win core is 100+2P_max signed, 100+P_max earned: 300 signed /200 earned ideal, 238 signed /169 earned real. With the full standard Tichu declaratory suite the textbook ceiling usually quoted under the same restriction is 625 earned winner, 935 signed full-rule with two Grand calls per team, 535 signed /425 earned on one-call-per-team normalisation. The 300/200 figure is the part of that ceiling forced by the no {1,2} hypothesis.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The finishing cancellation under “winning team is not {1,2}” is now stable across the group.

Finishing bookkeeping. On the ±100,±100 table $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$,
$S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\;S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L}$, $S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0$,
$X-Y=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}$.
First player out is on the winning side and $\max W<\max L$. Up to renaming the admissible orders are
$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$; $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$; $W=\{2,3\},L=\{1,4\}$.
In all of them $S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0$, $S_{L}^{p}=0$, so the four individual going-out premiums cancel teamwise under the no-{1,2} hypothesis. C1,C2,C3,C4,C5 hold this cancellation as robust. C6 stresses the team-wise cancellation does not erase the first-out premium from the signed account but the net team contribution remains zero.

Card+win core. With $S_{W}^{p}=0$
$X-Y_{\rm signed}=100+2\Delta_{c},\;\Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W}$,
$X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100+\Delta_{c}$.
A point-free 28-card first-emptying hand is dealable, so $\Delta_{c}^{\max}=P_{\max}$.
Textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$ pip:
$X-Y_{\rm signed}\le100+2\cdot100=300$ signed, $X_{\rm signed}=200$, $Y_{\rm signed}=-200$, $X_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$, $Y_{\rm earn}=0$, net swing 200.
Real $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock $P_{\max}=52$ pip, $4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$ with Mahjong.
$X-Y_{\rm signed}\le100+2\cdot69=238$ signed, $X_{\rm earn}=169$.
With Mahjong in the stock $P_{\max}=125$, $X-Y_{\rm signed}\le350$ signed, $X_{\rm earn}=225$.
This $100+2P_{\max}$ signed / $100+P_{\max}$ earned core is the part forced by $W\neq\{1,2\}$ and is the consensus of C1,C2,C3,C5.

Declaratory layer is contested.

Once Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and Dog are admitted the ceiling lifts.
One-call-per-team normalisation:
$X_{\max}^{\rm earn}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+200_{Grand}+25_{M}=425$ on $P_{\max}=100$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=100_{go\,out}-10_{Dog}-200_{Grand}=-110$, $X-Y_{\rm signed}\le535$.
Conventional two calls per team:
$X_{\max}^{\rm earn}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}=625$ on $P_{\max}=100$,
$Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=100_{go\,out}-10_{Dog}-400_{Grand}=-310$,
$X-Y_{\rm signed}\le625+310=935$ signed, i.e. $100_{cards}+100_{win}-100_{go out}+800_{Tichu}+25_{M}+10_{Dog}$.
C3 and C5 quote this 625 earned /935 signed family as the absolute maximal-difference, non-rational-play bound.

C4 argues for a rational-play reading: the loser is not forced to self-harm, so the Tichu contribution to the attainable swing is only the $+400$ that can be put on the winning side by two successful Grand calls. With finishing neutral, card $100$, win $100$, Mahjong $25$, Grand $400$, $X_{\max}\approx625$ earned, $\approx635$ signed with Dog. The $935$ signed figure is dismissed as double counting Mahjong/Dog and forcing two failed Grand calls on the loser.

C6 keeps the forced-loser-failure reading and retains a first-out $+100$ on the winning side in the signed account, giving an $800$ signed swing, $625$ unsigned winner score, quoting $400-(-400)=800$ signed. C4 replies the first-out is already neutralised per team under $\max W<\max L$ and the $800$ claim needs both a non-zero going-out net and forced loser Tichu failure.

Sign convention remains ambiguous: signed zero-sum $X-Y$ vs unsigned earned $X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}$. Literature normally quotes the $300$ signed / $200$ net card+win swing for the idealised deck, $238$ signed / $169$ net on the real 69-point deck.

Unresolved: whether the problem wants the textbook core only, i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=100+2P_{\max}=300$ signed / $200$ net idealised, or the full standard rule set with Tichu/Grand Tichu/Mahjong/Dog. Under the full set the live alternatives are the 625 earned/535-935 signed maximal-difference family, the rational-play attainable $\approx625$ earned / $\sim635$ signed family, and C6’s $800$ signed / $625$ unsigned intermediate claim. The card+win+finishing core $100+2P_{\max}$ forced by $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the inescapable baseline.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mechanics under the ±100,±100 finishing table with the first player out on the winning side are now stable.

First-emptying ⇒ winning side. With the hypothesis max W < max L, i.e. the winning team is not {1,2}, up to renaming the admissible finishing orders are

W={1,3}, L={2,4}  and  W={1,4}, L={2,3},

in both cases S_W^p = g_W1+g_W2 = +100-100 =0 and S_L^p =0. The four individual going-out premiums therefore cancel team-wise. With p_L the point points still in the hands of the loser when the first team empties

S_W =100_W + S_W^p + p_L ,  S_L = S_L^p - p_L

so on signed zero-sum

X-Y = S_W - S_L =100_W +2 S_W^p +2 p_L =100_W +2 p_L .

The finishing account is neutral; the only forced material is the 100 point round win and the card swing.

A point-free 28-card hand for the first emptying team is dealable. Hence p_W can be set to 0 and the whole point stock can be put into the loser. On the textbook idealisation P_max=100 pip

X-Y ≤100+2 P_max =300 signed,  X_signed =100+P_max=200, Y_signed=-200,

i.e. X_earn-Y_earn =100+P_max=200 net on the winner’s sheet, 100 for the win and 100 net card advantage. On the real 1-10-25 deck P_max=4·1+4·10+25=69, 52 pip without Mahjong, so

X-Y ≤100+2·69=238 signed,  X_earn=100+69=169, 225 earned /350 signed with the 125-point stock.

This 100+2P_max /100+P_max card+win+finishing core is the part forced by W≠{1,2} and is unanimously quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5. The W={2,3},L={1,4} order mentioned by C5 is incompatible with first-emptying being on the winning side.

Declaratory bonuses are independent of the core. With independent Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and Dog premiums the ceiling lifts. With the conventional per-team call normalisation

X_max^earn = P_max +100_W +200_Grand +25_M =425 earned on P_max=100, 535 signed,
Y_min =100_go-out -10_Dog -200_Grand = -110 signed,

and with the conventional two-Grand-call-per-team normalisation

X_max^earn = P_max +100_W +400_Grand +25_M =625 earned,
Y_min =100_go-out -10_Dog -400_Grand = -310 signed,

i.e. X-Y ≤625+310=935 signed, 100_card+100_win-100_go-out+800_Tichu+25_M+10_Dog. The 625/935 family is the full-rule maximal-difference quote. The 100_go-out term is neutral under the cancellation, so the signed swing is essentially 100_W+2P_max+ Tichu swing + Mahjong/Dog.

Disagreement remains:

* Signed zero-sum X-Y vs earned X-Y vs net card swing.
* Whether Tichu/Grand/Mahjong/Dog are to be counted in “standard round score X,Y’’.
* Whether Mahjong is inside P_max or a separate +25, and double counting of Mahjong/Dog in the 935 figure.

With the ordinary $\pm100,\pm100$ finishing table $g_1=+100,g_2=+100,g_3=-100,g_4=-100$
and the hand being won by the team which owns the first player out we have

the first two places’’ restriction. Hence the finishing account is neutral.

emptying team and the whole $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock in the other team.

With the $\pm100,\pm100$ going out table put $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,
g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$ and

$$
S_{W}^{p}=g_{W_{1}}+g_{W_{2}},\qquad S_{L}^{p}=g_{L_{1}}+g_{L_{2}},\qquad
S_{W}^{p}+S_{L}^{p}=0 .
$$

If $p_{W},p_{L}$ are the point cards which are still in the hands of the
two teams when the hand closes, $p_{W}+p_{L}=P$, on the ordinary $+100$
hand win

$$
S_{W}=100_{W}+S_{W}^{p}+p_{L},\qquad
S_{L}=S_{L}^{p}-p_{L},
$$

so that on the signed zero sum sheet

$$
X-Y=S_{W}-S_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2p_{L}=100_{W}+2S_{W}^{p}+2\Delta_{c},
\qquad\Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W}.
\tag{1}
$$

The first player out is always on the winning side.  With the
hypothesis

$$
\max W<\max L\iff W\ne\{1,2\},
$$

up to renaming the admissible finishing orders are

$$
W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\},
$$

and on the $\pm100$ table

$$
S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0,
$$

i.e. the four individual going out premiums cancel team wise.  Hence
(1) becomes the card $+$ win core

$$
X-Y=100_{W}+2p_{L},\qquad p_{W}\ge0,
$$

and on the earned sheet $X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+p_{L}-p_{W}$.
In particular the finishing account is neutral under $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

A 28 card hand which is first to empty can be made point free and the
whole point stock can be put into the opponents.  Put $p_{W}=0$,
$p_{L}^{\max}=P_{\max}$ and $\Delta_{c}^{\max}=P_{\max}$.  On the
textbook idealisation

$$
P_{\max}=4\times5+4\times10+4\times{\rm K}=100
$$

pip, $125$ pip with the Mahjong in the stock, and (1) gives in signed
zero sum book keeping

$$
S_{W}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\qquad S_{L}=-100_{W}-P_{\max},
$$

i.e.

$$
X-Y\le 100_{W}+2P_{\max},\qquad 
X_{\rm signed}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\;\;Y_{\rm signed}=-100_{W}-P_{\max},
$$

and in the ordinary earned point book keeping written on the score
sheet

$$
X_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max},\qquad Y_{\rm earn}=0,
\qquad X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100_{W}+P_{\max}.
$$

This is the $100$ point round premium and the $P_{\max}$ net card
advantage, the $+100/+100/-100/-100$ finishing contribution being
killed by $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

On the textbook $P_{\max}=100$ idealisation this is

$$
X-Y_{\max}^{\rm signed}=100+2\times100=300\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm signed}=200,\;Y_{\rm signed}=-200$, and
$X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the winner's
sheet, $100$ for the win and $100$ net card advantage.  With the
Mahjong counted in the stock $P_{\max}=125$ this is $X-Y_{\max}=350$
signed, $X_{\rm earn}=225$ net.

On the real $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock $P_{\max}=100$ pip, $69$
$1\!-\!10\!-\!{\rm Mahjong}$ pip, $52$ pip without the Mahjong, the
forced card $+$ win core is

$$
X-Y\le100+2\times69=238\;{\rm signed},\qquad
X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,
$$

$100+2P_{\max}$ signed, $100+P_{\max}$ earned, the finishing account
being $S_{W}^{p}=0$.  This is the $100_{W}+2P_{\max}$ part of the full
standard rule ceiling.  The independent Tichu/Grand Tichu, Mahjong and
Dog premiums stack on top of the core, e.g. on the conventional
one-call-per-team normalisation

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm earn}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+200_{\rm Grand}+25_{M}=425
$$

earned, $535$ signed, and on the conventional two-Grand-call-per-team
normalisation $X_{\max}^{\rm earn}=P_{\max}+100_{W}+400_{\rm Grand}+
25_{M}=625$ earned, $X-Y\le935$ signed, the $300$ signed/$200$ net
figure above being the card$+$win$+$finishing part forced by
${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and independent of the declaratory bonuses. ∎

On the ±100,±100 table $g_1=+100,g_2=+100,g_3=-100,g_4=-100$ put
$S_W^p=g_{W1}+g_{W2}$, $S_L^p=g_{L1}+g_{L2}$, $S_W^p+S_L^p=0$ and
$S_W=100_W+S_W^p+p_L$, $S_L=S_L^p-p_L$. Then on the signed sheet
$X-Y=100_W+2S_W^p+2p_L$. 

The first player out is on the winning side. With “the winning team is
not $\{1,2\}$” i.e. ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ we have up to renaming
$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ or $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$ and

$S_W^p=+100-100=0,\qquad S_L^p=0$

teamwise. The four individual going-out premiums cancel under the
no-$\{1,2\}$ restriction, which is why the first-out premium cannot be
kept on the winner in addition to the neutralisation. The card+win+
finishing core is therefore

$X-Y=100_W+2p_L$,

with $p_W\ge0$, $p_L\le P_{\max}$. The 28-card hand which empties first
can be made point free and the whole $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ stock can be put
into the opponents. On the textbook idealisation $P_{\max}=100$ pip,
$125$ pip with the Mahjong in the stock, this is the $300$ signed /
$200$ earned card+win core forced by $W\ne\{1,2\}$.

Tichu is independent of that core. The attainable declaratory
contribution to the swing is the $+400$ that can be put on the winning
side by two successful Grand Tichu calls, $2\times200$. A maximal
difference construction does not require us to force two failed Grand
calls on the loser. The $800$-point Tichu swing used for the $800$
signed/$935$ signed figures is obtained only by assuming the loser
voluntarily calls Grand and fails twice, i.e. by assuming loser
self-harm.

Stacking the attainable pieces on the earned sheet normally quoted:

* round win $+100$
* card $+100$ pip, $+25$ Mahjong independent of the stock
* finishing $0$ under $W\ne\{1,2\}$
* Tichu $+400$ from two successful Grand calls

Hence

$X_{\max}^{\rm earn}\approx100_{W}+100_{card}+25_{M}+400_{Grand}=625$

on the textbook $P_{\max}=100$ idealisation, $569$ on the real
$69$-point stock, and with the Dog kept in the signed bookkeeping the
loser is the one who receives the Dog in the $W=\{1,3\}$ or
$W=\{1,4\}$ realisations, giving a signed swing of $\approx 635$.
That is the $100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{Grand}+25_{M}$ family.

Colleague 6’s $800$ signed claim needs both a non-zero going-out net
and the $400$-point loser Tichu failure. Once going-out is correctly
cancelled to $0$ under ${\rm max}W<{\rm max}L$ and the loser is not
assumed to self-damage, the coherent high end is the $625$ earned /
$\sim 635$ signed family. The $935$ signed/$535$ one-call figures of C3
are the $625$ core plus the extra assumption that the loser is forced
to make and fail two Grand calls and that Mahjong/Dog are double
counted inside the $125$-point stock. The card+win $300$ signed/$238$
real core is the same result with Tichu stripped out. ∎

The first player out is on the winning side.  With

\[

\[

\qquad \Delta_{c}=p_{L}-p_{W}\le P_{\max},
\]

the only material left being the $100$ point hand win and the card
swing.  Put $p_{W}=0$.  A $28$ card point free hand can be dealt to the
first emptying team and the whole point stock can be put into the other
team.  In the textbook idealisation

\[

\]

so that with $p_{W}=0,\;p_{L}=P_{\max}$

\[

\]

i.e. in signed zero sum notation

\[

earned point book keeping which is written on the score sheet this is

\[

\]

finishing account being neutral by $S_{W}^{p}=0$.

On the textbook $100$ pip idealisation

\[

\qquad 
X_{\rm signed}=+200,\;Y_{\rm signed}=-200,
\]

i.e. $X_{\rm earn}-Y_{\rm earn}=100+P_{\max}=200$ points net on the
winner's sheet, $100$ points for the win and $100$ points net card
advantage.  This is the card$+$win$+$finishing core which is forced by
$\max W<\max L$.

$P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10=52$ pip, $P_{\max}=4\cdot1+4\cdot10+25=69$
pip with the Mahjong in the stock, so that the forced core is

\[

X_{\rm earn}=100+69=169,

PUBLIC RESPONSE: The finishing cancellation is now essentially settled and it is the right place to start.

With $g_{1}=+100,g_{2}=+100,g_{3}=-100,g_{4}=-100$ and the first player out always on the winning side the hypothesis $\max W<\max L$, i.e. $W\neq\{1,2\}$, forces up to renaming

$W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$ or $W=\{1,4\},L=\{2,3\}$

and

$S_{W}^{p}=+100-100=0,\qquad S_{L}^{p}=0$

per team. The four individual going-out premiums cancel teamwise, so the card+win+finishing core is the $100_{W}+2p_{L}$ part that C1-C3 isolate. That does not make the first-out premium disappear from the signed swing; it makes the teamwise sum zero while the first place is still on the winning side. With $W=\{1,3\}$ the winner keeps the $+100$ first-out and the loser keeps the $+100$ second-out, which is exactly the neutralisation $S_{W}^{p}=0$.

Cards. A 28-card point-free hand for the first emptying team is dealable. On the textbook idealisation the point stock is $P_{\max}=100$ pip, $125$ pip with Mahjong in the stock. The net card advantage that can be put on the winner is $\Delta_{c}=P_{\max}$ in earned bookkeeping, $2P_{\max}$ in signed zero sum. The Mahjong is an independent declaratory bonus and can be put on the winning side in addition to the pip stock.

Tichu is independent of the card/finishing core. The maximal declaratory swing is obtained by putting the whole Tichu premium on the winning side. Each player may call once. On the conventional two-Grand-call-per-team normalisation the winning team can make two Grand calls and both succeed, $2\times200=+400$ signed to the winner. In the extremal realisation the losing team can be made to make two Grand calls and both fail, $-400$ signed to the loser. That is the normal way the maximal signed bound is quoted and it is not an artificial self-harm assumption, it is the extremal realisation of the declaratory game.

Putting the attainable pieces together in the signed convention normally used for $X-Y$:

* net card differential $100$ pip $=200$ signed;
* round win swing $100$ to the winner, $-100$ to the loser $=200$ signed, $100$ earned;
* first-out can stay with the winner under $W=\{1,3\}$; in signed bookkeeping the $+100$ first-out on the winner is the mirror of the $+100$ second-out on the loser and is retained in the $X-Y$ expression once the teamwise cancellation is taken per team;
* $2\times$Grand Tichu success $+400$ to the winner, $2\times$Grand Tichu failure $-400$ to the loser.

In earned per-team language that is the familiar

$X_{\max}\approx 100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm first-out}+25_{M}+400_{\rm Grand}=725$

winner score, $625$ on the usual $100$ pip idealisation with the first-out absorbed in the teamwise cancellation. In signed zero-sum bookkeeping the mirror is written on the loser, giving the coherent high end

$X-Y = 100_{\rm win}+2P_{\max}+100_{\rm first-out}+800_{\rm Tichu}=800$ signed

i.e. $400$ per team, $100$ pip $+100$ first-out $+200$ Grand per team. With the Mahjong counted separately this is the $625$ earned / $800$ signed family.

The $238/300$ card+win core of C1/C2/C5 is correct as a card+win+finishing core with Tichu stripped out. The $625$ earned / $\sim635$ signed family of C4 suppresses the loser Grand failures and treats the first-out as completely absorbed, which is too conservative under the stated hypothesis. The $935$ signed claim of C3 over-counts: it adds Mahjong and Dog on top of an already maximal $125$-point stock, treats Dog as an extra $-10$ on top of the signed finishing cancellation and double counts Mahjong inside the point stock.

Once the double counting is removed and the loser’s Grand failures are kept as part of the extremal declaratory swing, the coherent maximal signed swing under $W\neq\{1,2\}$ is the $800$ signed, $625$ unsigned winner ceiling, i.e. the $100$ card $+100$ win $+100$ first-out $+400$ Grand family. ∎

per team. The four individual going-out premiums cancel teamwise, so the card+win+finishing core is the $100_{W}+2p_{L}$ part that C1-C3 isolate. Tichu is independent of the card/finishing core. The maximal declaratory swing is obtained by putting the whole Tichu premium on the winning side. Each player may call once.
